title: Lab Safety Scenario Analysis: Make the Safe Call
originality: All scenarios, prompts, answer explanations, and layout are original.

scenarios.title: Goggles on Standby
scenarios.text: Maya begins measuring a dilute solution while her splash goggles rest on her forehead. Her partner is still collecting materials.
scenarios.evidence: Chemical measuring has begun while Maya's goggles are on her forehead.
scenarios.risk: A splash could reach unprotected eyes.
scenarios.action: Stop measuring and wear splash goggles correctly before continuing.
scenarios.why: The eye barrier must be in place before exposure can occur.

scenarios.title: Blocked Aisle
scenarios.text: Two backpacks and a charging cable cross the aisle between a lab table and the exit.
scenarios.evidence: Backpacks and a cable cross a travel route leading toward the exit.
scenarios.risk: Someone could trip, and movement during an emergency could be delayed.
scenarios.action: Stop traffic through the area and move the items to the assigned storage location.
scenarios.why: Removing the obstruction eliminates the trip hazard and keeps the exit route accessible.

scenarios.title: Mystery Beaker
scenarios.text: An unlabeled beaker containing a clear liquid is left beside the balance. No one in the group knows who placed it there.
scenarios.evidence: The beaker has no label, and no one can identify the clear liquid.
scenarios.risk: Touching or testing an unknown substance could cause exposure or contamination.
scenarios.action: Do not touch or test it; keep others away and notify the teacher immediately.
scenarios.why: Avoiding contact prevents additional exposure while the teacher secures and identifies the material by site procedure.

scenarios.title: Heating Direction
scenarios.text: Eli warms a test tube while its opening points toward the student across the table.
scenarios.evidence: The opening of a heated test tube points toward another person.
scenarios.risk: Hot liquid or vapor could eject toward that person.
scenarios.action: Stop heating; use the teacher-approved holder and point the opening away from all people.
scenarios.why: Stopping removes the immediate energy input, and safe orientation reduces direct exposure if material ejects.

scenarios.title: Broken Glass
scenarios.text: A cracked graduated cylinder breaks in the sink. A student reaches toward the pieces with a bare hand.
scenarios.evidence: Broken glass is in the sink, and a bare hand is reaching toward it.
scenarios.risk: Sharp glass could cut the student.
scenarios.action: Do not pick it up by hand; alert the teacher and follow the designated broken-glass procedure.
scenarios.why: The designated tools and container prevent direct hand contact and isolate sharp waste.

scenarios.title: Extra Reagent
scenarios.text: After pouring too much reagent, a student prepares to return the excess to the stock bottle.
scenarios.evidence: Previously poured reagent is about to be returned to the stock container.
scenarios.risk: The stock chemical could be contaminated, affecting later safety and results.
scenarios.action: Do not return it; ask the teacher for the correct waste procedure.
scenarios.why: Keeping used material out of the stock bottle protects the shared supply from contamination.

scenarios.title: Hair Near Heat
scenarios.text: During burner setup, long loose hair hangs close to the work area and one sleeve is not secured.
scenarios.evidence: Loose hair and clothing are near a burner setup.
scenarios.risk: Hair or clothing could contact heat or flame and ignite or cause a burn.
scenarios.action: Turn off or do not light the heat source; secure hair and loose clothing first.
scenarios.why: Removing the ignition exposure before heating prevents contact with flame or hot equipment.

scenarios.title: Direct Smell
scenarios.text: A student lifts an open container toward the nose to identify its odor without teacher direction.
scenarios.evidence: The open container is being raised directly toward the student's nose without instruction.
scenarios.risk: A concentrated vapor could be inhaled.
scenarios.action: Move away, close the container if safe and directed, and ask the teacher; only waft when specifically instructed.
scenarios.why: Increasing distance and following teacher direction limits unnecessary inhalation exposure.

scenarios.title: Splash Report
scenarios.text: A small splash reaches a student's forearm. The student wipes it with a paper towel and says there is no need to interrupt class.
scenarios.evidence: A chemical reached skin, but the student only wiped it and did not report the exposure.
scenarios.risk: Chemical may remain on the skin, and delaying the correct response could increase injury.
scenarios.action: Alert the teacher immediately while beginning the room's designated skin-exposure rinse, unless the posted site/SDS procedure specifies otherwise.
scenarios.why: Rapid rinsing limits contact time while immediate reporting activates the correct site-specific response.

scenarios.title: Hot Plate Left On
scenarios.text: A group finishes early and leaves the station while the hot plate remains on beside scattered papers.
scenarios.evidence: An energized hot plate is unattended beside paper.
scenarios.risk: Someone could be burned, or nearby combustible material could ignite.
scenarios.action: Remain at the station. If trained and it is safe, use the normal control to turn off the hot plate; keep others clear and alert the teacher if it cannot be shut down safely.
scenarios.why: Immediate safe shutdown removes the heat source, while guarding the area prevents contact or ignition during escalation.
